risks: Any disruption in these lease arrangements could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Any such disruption may adversely affect our ability to execute advertising campaigns, retain existing customers, attract new customers, or maintain our revenues.
Such events could require us to relocate or dismantle existing media sites, which may involve additional costs and operational disruptions.

Any material disruption in the availability of such leased sites or our inability to effectively manage and renew these arrangements could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Our reputation and brand recognition are important factors in attracting and retaining advertisers, advertising agencies, corporate customers and other clients, as well as in maintaining relationships with landowners, government authorities and other stakeholders.

Our ability to generate repeat business depends on the quality, timely execution and effective maintenance of our outdoor advertising media and our ability to deliver advertising campaigns in accordance with customer requirements.

Any failure to execute advertising campaigns in a timely manner, maintain the quality and visibility of our advertising media, comply with contractual obligations, or effectively manage client expectations may adversely affect customer satisfaction and our reputation.

Further, any damage to our brand arising from operational deficiencies, adverse publicity, disputes with customers, vendors or landowners, regulatory actions or any other unforeseen circumstances may reduce customer confidence, affect our ability to secure new business opportunities and adversely impact our business and financial performance.

compliance_legal.risk: To obtain a complete understanding, you should read this section in conjunction with the sections “Industry Overview”, “Our Business” and “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Position and Results of Operations” on pages 118, 153 and 210 of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, respectively.
Our business operates through outdoor advertising media sites that are installed on lands and premises obtained under lease or license arrangements from various third-party landowners.

The availability of such locations is subject to several factors beyond our control, including willingness of landowners to lease their properties, commercial negotiations, regulatory approvals, local municipal requirements, and competition from other outdoor advertising operators.

Since we do not own the underlying land on which our advertising structures are installed, we are exposed to risks associated with changes in land ownership, redevelopment of properties, regulatory actions affecting the leased locations, or other circumstances that may result in termination or modification of our lease arrangements.
Further, a part of our business involves operating advertising media pursuant to permissions, licences or advertising rights granted by municipal and other governmental authorities.

Our operations are exposed to various regional risks, including slowdown in economic activity, reduction in advertising expenditure by businesses, adverse changes in government policies, municipal regulations relating to outdoor advertising, changes in taxation or licensing requirements, political or social disturbances, natural disasters, extreme weather conditions, public health emergencies or any other events affecting business activities in Gujarat.

Any adverse regulatory developments, cancellation or non-renewal of permissions, restrictions imposed by municipal or other governmental authorities, or increased competition within the outdoor advertising industry in Gujarat may adversely affect our operations and growth prospects.
Our Company is party to certain legal proceeding.
Our Company is party to certain legal proceedings.
These legal proceedings are pending at different levels of adjudication before various courts and legal forums.
Even if we are successful in defending such cases, we will be subjected to legal and other costs relating to defending Page | 31 such litigation, and such costs could be substantial.
For further details, pertaining to material pending outstanding litigations involving our Company, see “Outstanding Litigations and Material Developments” on page 222. 6.

We require certain approvals and licenses in the ordinary course of business and are required to comply with certain rules and regulations to operate our business, any failure to obtain, retain and renew such approvals and licences or comply with such rules and regulations may adversely affect our operations.
The seasonal nature of our business also requires effective management of our working capital and advertising inventory.
Our business is dependent on the experience, expertise and continued services of our Directors and Key Managerial Personnel.

Our business has been developed under the guidance and leadership of our directors, who are responsible for formulating our business strategies, maintaining relationships with customers, landowners, advertising agencies, municipal and other governmental authorities, identifying new business opportunities, overseeing day-to-day operations and managing the overall growth of our Company.

The continued success of our business is dependent, to a significant extent, upon the experience, industry knowledge, business relationships and leadership of our Directors and Key Managerial Personnel.

The details of our directors are set out below: Page | 37 Name Position Brief Profile Harshit Hitendra Shah Managing Director Harshit Hitendra Shah, aged 34 years, is the Managing Director of our Company.
Amitkumar Govindbhai Patel Non - Executive Director Amitkumar Govindbhai Patel, aged 56 years, is the Promoter and Non-Executive Director of our Company.

He possesses over 15 years of entrepreneurial experience across diverse industries and has held leadership positions in various organizations, including serving as the Managing Director of Axita Cotton Limited.
As a Non-Executive Director, he provides strategic guidance and oversight on key business matters, while supporting the Board in formulating policies and driving the Company's sustainable growth.
Jimit Amitbhai Patel Non - Executive Director Jimit Amitbhai Patel, aged 25 years, is the Promoter and Non-Executive Director of our Company.
He holds a Diploma in Hotel Management from American Hotel & Lodging Educational Institute.

As a Promoter and Non-Executive Director, he provides strategic guidance to the Company and supports the Board in the formulation of business strategies, corporate governance matters and business development initiatives, contributing to the Company's long-term growth and strategic objectives.

financial_valuation.risk: If any of the following risks, or other risks that are not currently known or are now deemed immaterial, actually occur, our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition could be adversely affected, the trading price of our Equity Shares could decline, and as prospective investors, you may lose all or part of your investment.

Any non-renewal, premature termination, increase in lease rentals, change in commercial terms, disputes with landowners, or inability to renew or replace existing leased sites on commercially acceptable terms could result in the loss of strategic advertising locations.

We rely on the reputation of the “Aarish Outdoors” brand in Gujarat, and any damage to our reputation or inability to secure advertising rights through competitive tender processes could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

The loss of existing locations or failure to secure new locations through such tender processes could adversely affect our inventory of advertising media, revenue generation, growth prospects and overall business operations.

Page | 29 As our business growth is dependent upon maintaining the goodwill associated with the "Aarish Outdoors" brand and our ability to continue securing strategic advertising locations through competitive bidding and other arrangements, any adverse impact on our reputation or our ability to obtain such advertising rights may materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Any delay in the collection of such receivables may adversely affect our liquidity, working capital requirements, cash flows and financial condition.

Further, as disclosed under the chapter titled "Objects of the Offer – Working Capital Requirements" beginning on page 80 of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, our business projections indicate trade receivable days of approximately 112 days and 134 days for Fiscal 2027 and Fiscal 2028, respectively.

Any delay in the realization of receivables beyond the agreed credit period may result in increased working capital requirements and could require us to utilize internal accruals or external borrowings to finance our day-to-day operations.

In addition, any significant increase in our trade receivables without a corresponding improvement in collection efficiency may adversely affect our operating cash flows, limit our ability to fund future growth and expansion, increase our dependence on external financing and adversely impact our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows. 4.

Any adverse developments affecting the economy, regulatory environment or business conditions in Gujarat could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Consequently, any material adverse change in the business, economic or regulatory environment in Gujarat could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
This could adversely affect our business, cash flows, financial condition, and results of operation.

internal_operational.risk: Any disruption in these lease arrangements could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Any such disruption may adversely affect our ability to execute advertising campaigns, retain existing customers, attract new customers, or maintain our revenues.
Such events could require us to relocate or dismantle existing media sites, which may involve additional costs and operational disruptions.

Any material disruption in the availability of such leased sites or our inability to effectively manage and renew these arrangements could adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Our reputation and brand recognition are important factors in attracting and retaining advertisers, advertising agencies, corporate customers and other clients, as well as in maintaining relationships with landowners, government authorities and other stakeholders.

Our ability to generate repeat business depends on the quality, timely execution and effective maintenance of our outdoor advertising media and our ability to deliver advertising campaigns in accordance with customer requirements.

Any failure to execute advertising campaigns in a timely manner, maintain the quality and visibility of our advertising media, comply with contractual obligations, or effectively manage client expectations may adversely affect customer satisfaction and our reputation.

Further, any damage to our brand arising from operational deficiencies, adverse publicity, disputes with customers, vendors or landowners, regulatory actions or any other unforeseen circumstances may reduce customer confidence, affect our ability to secure new business opportunities and adversely impact our business and financial performance.

A significant portion of our current assets comprises trade receivables arising from advertising services provided to our customers, including corporate clients, advertising agencies and government authorities.
The outdoor advertising business generally involves extending credit to customers based on mutually agreed commercial terms.
Consequently, there is a time gap between the execution of advertising campaigns and the realization of payments from customers.
Accordingly, our business requires substantial working capital to support operations and finance the gap between the execution of advertising campaigns and the receipt of payments from customers.

The collection period for our receivables may vary depending upon the nature of customers, contractual credit terms, internal approval processes of customers, verification of invoices, completion of campaign-related documentation and, in certain cases, administrative procedures followed by government and institutional customers.

Further, if any of our customers delays payment, disputes the amounts billed, experiences financial difficulties or defaults on its payment obligations, our cash flows and liquidity may be adversely affected.
During the periods indicated below, 82.01 %, 88.30 % and 63.89 % for Fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024 of our revenue from operations was generated from customers located in Gujarat.

If we fail to comply with all applicable regulations or if the regulations governing our business or their implementation change, we may incur increased costs, be subject to penalties or suffer a disruption in our business activities, any of which could adversely affect our results of operations.

Any disruption in the availability of suitable advertising sites may result in delays in execution of advertising campaigns, loss of customers, reduction in revenues and may materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Any structural failure, collapse, detachment of display materials or other malfunction of our advertising media may result in personal injury or loss of life, damage to public or private property, disruption of traffic or other public inconvenience.

If any of our Directors or Key Managerial Personnel are unable or unwilling to continue with our Company due to resignation, retirement, incapacity or any other reason, or if we are unable to attract, retain or replace such personnel with individuals possessing comparable experience, expertise and industry relationships within a reasonable period, our business operations, customer relationships, strategic initiatives and future growth prospects may be adversely affected.
Further, the loss of their services may result in the loss of key business relationships, disruption in decision-making processes and delays in the execution of our business strategies.

In the event of such termination or non-renewal, we may be required to relocate our offices, service centers, or employee residences, which could result in significant costs, administrative inconveniences, and potential disruption to our business operations. 22.

The delay in statutory filings was due to a combination of factors, including technical issues on regulatory portals and disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, which impacted internal coordination and processing timelines.

Any significant uninsured or underinsured loss, or any prolonged disruption to our operations arising from events not adequately covered by insurance, may materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Any increase in employee attrition or shortage of skilled personnel may result in higher recruitment and training costs, operational inefficiencies and disruption of our business activities.

Since these vendors and contractors operate independently and are not under our direct control, we are exposed to risks arising from their operational inefficiencies, financial condition, labour shortages, non-availability of raw materials, equipment failures, transportation disruptions, non-performance, delays in execution or any other factors beyond our control.

Any continued or future slowdown in the Indian economy or a further increase in inflation could have a material adverse effect on the price of our raw materials and demand for our products and, as a result, on our business and financial results.

strategy_growth.risk: We may be unable to sufficiently obtain, maintain, protect, or enforce our intellectual property and other proprietary rights.
As on date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, we have applied for the registration of trademark “ ” under class 35 of the Trademarks Act, 1999.
The said trademark application has been objected to by the Trade Marks Registry and is presently pending adjudication before the relevant authority.
There can be no assurance that the objection will be successfully overcome or that the trademark registration will be granted within the expected timeline or at all.

Pending the registration of these trademarks, any third party may use the above-mentioned trademarks and we may have a lesser recourse to initiate legal proceedings to protect our intellectual property.
Further, our applications for the registration of trademarks may be opposed by third parties, and we may have to incur significant cost in relation to these oppositions.

In the event we are not able to obtain registrations due to opposition by third parties or if any injunctive or other adverse order is issued against us in respect of any of our trademarks for which we have applied for registration, we may not be able to use such trademarks and / or avail the legal protection or prevent unauthorized use of such trademarks by third parties, which may adversely affect our goodwill and business.
For further details see “Our Business - Intellectual Property” and “Government and Other Statutory Approvals” on pages 153 and 228, respectively of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus. 8.
The advertising industry has witnessed increasing adoption of digital marketing channels, social media platforms, online video, influencer marketing and other technology-driven advertising solutions.
Any interruption, failure or security breach of our information technology systems may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Our business operations are dependent on information technology systems for various functions, including customer relationship management, campaign planning, billing, accounting, financial reporting, communication, maintenance of business records and other administrative and operational activities.

Our information technology systems may be vulnerable to disruptions arising from hardware or software failures, computer viruses, malware, ransomware, cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data corruption, telecommunications failures, power outages, human errors or other unforeseen events.

While the current government has announced that its general intention is to continue India’s economic liberalisation and deregulation policies, there can be no assurance that such policies will be continued and the rate of economic liberalisation could change affecting foreign investments and foreign exchange controls among others.

India’s economic growth is affected by various factors including domestic consumption and savings, balance of trade movements, namely export demand and movements in key imports (oil and oil products), global economic uncertainty and liquidity crisis, volatility in exchange currency rates and annual rainfall which affects agricultural production.

These factors include interest rates, rates of economic growth, fiscal and monetary policies of governments, inflation, deflation, foreign exchange fluctuations, consumer credit availability, fluctuations in commodities markets, consumer debt levels, unemployment trends and other matters that influence consumer confidence, spending and tourism.

Any adverse revisions to India’s credit ratings international debt by international rating agencies may adversely affect our ability to raise additional overseas financing and the interest rates and other commercial terms at which such additional financing Page | 53 is available.

Under the foreign exchange regulations currently in force in India, transfer of shares between non- residents and residents are freely permitted (subject to certain exceptions) if they comply with the pricing guidelines and reporting requirements specified by the RBI.

Additionally, shareholders who seek to convert the Rupee proceeds from a sale of shares in India into foreign currency and repatriate that foreign currency from India will require a no objection/ tax clearance certificate from the income tax authority.
